text:
infra-alerts (bot): ALERT · Elevated 5xx rate for /api/v1/generate in us-west-2 · 3m average 6.2% (baseline 0.3%)

alice (sre): seeing it too on the dashboard, spikes line up with heavier L4 ingress.

dinesh (oncall): paging in. taking primary. ETA 2m. any customer-facing impact?

eva (support): several tickets opened — users reporting timeouts and failed requests from our hosted API. Affected customers: 3 mid-market (billing alerts), multiple dev keys.

ben (runtime): initial hypothesis: request queueing at edge -> backend overload -> 502s from gateway. also possible a recent config rollback changed keepalive.

carla (observability): heads-up: traces are sparse for these requests, sampling looks like it dropped to 0.1% exactly when spike started. logs for the gateway are missing request-id headers for a subset of flows.

alice (sre): ok that's the crux — missing correlation IDs breaks our trace join. can we temporarily increase trace sampling and inject request-id?

carla (observability): I can flip sampling to 50% for the next 30m. also can enable request-id middleware at the LB level, but that needs a quick config and deploy (10min).

ben (runtime): I can push a zero-risk config change to insert X-Request-Id on ingress if we enable the header rewrite on the gateway. small nginx snippet:
```
proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $request_id;
```
We'll need a restart for the proxy though — can do a rolling restart to avoid downtime.

alice (sre): before restarting, let's add a stopgap: duplicate traffic to a secondary path? maybe enable fallback pool that routes to dedicated instances (non-autoscaled) to absorb traffic.

dinesh (oncall): agree. Ben — can you open a short-lived canary route to dedicated-pool-west? If latency behaves, we'll shift 20% of traffic.

ben (runtime): spinning up route now. command: `rctl route create --from ingress --to dedicated-pool-west --weight 20`

deploy-bot (bot): route create job queued · job id job-8492 · estimated apply 18s

ben (runtime): applied. monitoring switch: keep an eye on token latency p50/p95, and 5xx.

carla (observability): sampling bumped to 50% at 1958889185. traces started appearing — many show 502 at gateway layer where upstream responded with 504 timeout. Also noticed an uptick in long tail on kv-cache MISS around 300–700ms for these traces.

eva (support): updating customers in Slack and sending a short incident note to affected accounts (ETA 15m for mitigation).

alice (sre): thoughts on cause: either upstream worker thread saturation (KV backend) or an N+1 in model-serving causing long tails. Ben, any recent deploys or config flips near timestamp 1958889000?

ben (runtime): last deploy to model-pool was 1958888700, small perf patch. No config flips to KV. But autoscaler did a scale-in event ~1958889050—interesting. Could be reactive scale-in chasing low CPU but elevated queue length.

carla (observability): current metrics: node CPU 45%, queue length increased 4x, connection pool exhaustion signs on model-pool. No per-request logs for ~30% of requests — likely missing request-id injection during LB->backend path.

alice (sre): immediate mitigation checklist:
- increase model-pool min replicas by +30% (prevent scale-in thrash)
- enable route fallback (done) and monitor 5xx trend
- flip request-id injection (canary)
- raise trace sampling to 100% for 10m if needed
- add short-term debug logs at gateway for missing headers (retain 1h)

ben (runtime): executing scale: `infra scale set model-pool --min 8` (was 6).

deploy-bot (bot): scale job started · job-8507

ben (runtime): scale applied. also adding header rewrite canary to a subset of ingress instances to minimize risk. plan: enable on 2/10 hosts, watch logs.

carla (observability): I've enabled 100% sampling at 1958889250 for 5m window. traces now show correlation across services for the new path. We see request-id present for canary route but missing for ~25% of old path requests.

alice (sre): good. if header injection fixes traceability, we'll confirm it's a gap in older edge proxies that missed the $request_id variable.

dinesh (oncall): handoff note: I'm going offline in 20m. leaving incident in active state. Next on-call: ben -> alice. Ben will take lead if anything escalates.

ben (runtime): noted. Will monitor for 30m. If 5xx > 1% for >5m, escalate to paging all-hands.

carla (observability): added a transient logship rule to capture 1% of requests that are missing X-Request-Id with an extended payload (headers + trace id) to a hot index for 1h retention:
```
if not req.headers['X-Request-Id']:
  emit debug: {path, upstream, conn_state, trace_id}
```
This will let us map offending proxies.

eva (support): posted status update to customers: "We are mitigating elevated errors; routing a portion of traffic to a fallback pool while we gather traces and apply temporary configuration. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alice (sre): early results: 5xx dropped from 6.2% -> 1.8% after route shift and scale-up. Not ideal but trending down.

carla (observability): discovered outlier: two edge hosts (ingress-7, ingress-9) had a kernel param change that removed `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse` enabling earlier ephemeral port reuse — causing premature connection resets under burst. Logs show resets correlated with missing headers.

ben (runtime): good find. rolling-restart of ingress-7 and ingress-9 with corrected sysctl. Command: `infra ssh ingress-7 -- sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1 && systemctl restart ingress-proxy`

deploy-bot (bot): restart job queued · job-8510

alice (sre): restart complete for ingress-7 and ingress-9. Monitoring.

carla (observability): after restarts and header injection canary → 5xx now 0.6% at 1958889400. Traces restored, request-id present for >98% of traffic.

dinesh (oncall): thanks team. leaving a concise handoff in PagerDuty:
- issue: transient ingress connection resets + autoscaler scale-in -> increased 5xx/504s
- mitigation: scaled model-pool min, route fallback 20%, sysctl rollback on two hosts, request-id injection canary, increased trace sampling, short-lived debug logs
- customer impact: partial failures for ~25m across several customers; currently degrading to near baseline; support messages sent
- follow-ups: add automated check for sysctl drift on ingress config, tighten autoscaler policy to consider queue length, add grooming ticket to make request-id injection permanent in ingress path

eva (support): I'll post final customer update and attach the timeline + mitigation actions.

alice (sre): creating follow-up tickets:
- #INC-3492: root-cause analysis & config drift fix (owner: alice)
- #INC-3493: autoscaler heuristic change (owner: ben)
- #INC-3494: permanent request-id injection + test (owner: carla)

ben (runtime): thumbs up. leaving monitoring on for 1h.

carla (observability): turning down 100% sampling at 1958889450 back to baseline 5% and removing the hot debug index (retained artifacts archived).

dinesh (oncall): handoff complete. All on-call, please watch error budget dashboards. If we regress, poke this thread. :eyes:

alice (sre): thanks everyone. closing incident thread unless new alerts reappear. :white_check_mark:
